## TL;DR

I QA'd the Agents page routing tab for missing-key and provider-failure wording and for the recent-decisions list, using fixtures in headless WebKit and jsdom only. Two copy defects were real and are fixed: a failed decisions request showed "Nothing recorded yet", which is a false empty state, and a blocked decision leaked an internal reason code into the note. I also aligned a WebKit fixture with the wording the server actually returns, so the render test now checks what users see. The QA write-up is in `docs/qa/2026-11-routing-failure-copy-qa.md`. Keys stayed masked throughout, and no real key was read or printed.

## Work and rationale

The previous QA pass (#1223) had already covered layout at three widths. This pass checked words. I traced each piece of user-facing failure copy from its server source to the screen: `modelRoutingStatus` and `probeModelRouting` in `runtime.ts`, the blocked-decision message in `policy.ts`, provider errors in `providers.ts`, and the panel's fallback and empty-state text in `ModelRoutingPanel.vue`.

The decisions-load defect was the most important. `refreshDecisions` caught every error and set the list to `[]`, and the template then showed "Nothing recorded yet." An outage therefore read as an empty history. I added a `decisionsError` ref. A failed load now shows an explicit notice with a Try again button, and a successful empty load keeps the original empty copy. Both states are tested. I chose a plain notice with a retry over a toast because the list is the only place that needs the signal.

The blocked-decision message read "Model routing could not decide (provider-failure) …". I mapped each fallback reason to a plain cause phrase in `policy.ts` and kept the next step. The only existing test checks the reason code, not the message, so the wording change was safe. The new test asserts that no slug appears.

The missing-key WebKit fixture used hand-written copy, "No TypeSafe Jev API key is saved yet — paste one below." The server returns "Save your TypeSafe Jev API key below (stored in .env only)." I changed the fixture and its assertion to the server's exact text, so the render check tests real wording.

I checked the rest without finding defects. The live "not configured" hint says "above", which is correct because the key form sits above the probe buttons. The fallback sentences read as normal behaviour, not as errors. An all-failure list renders each row with the fallback sentence and no error banner. The Jev key field is a password input, and provider errors contain no key values.

I added three WebKit cases for the failed-load state at 375, 768 and 1280 px and jsdom tests for the failed load, the retry, the real empty state and an all-failure list. I did not add a separate WebKit fixture for an all-failure list; the jsdom test covers its copy, and the existing mixed-list render check still passes.

## Approaches tried

I first considered asserting the missing-key and failure wording only in jsdom. That would have missed what the browser actually renders, so I kept the WebKit fixture path and extended it. The first WebKit run failed in `beforeAll` because the built stylesheet was absent, not because of any copy. `bun run build:ui` fixed it, and the suite then passed 15 of 15 with real WebKit.

I also tried running vitest directly with `bunx vitest run` on the panel test. It failed to load the `.vue` file because the root config does not load the Vue plugin. The repo's `bun run test` wrapper runs the same tests correctly, so I used the wrapper.

## Challenges and blockers

The first scoped `repoos check` failed on one test in `src/ui-app/tests/agent-review.test.ts` (#0101, "gates follow-up creation before the freeze"). The assertion received "Task #0001 is waiting for automatic review to finish" where it expected a needs-some-work review message. That file is about review gating and does not touch routing copy. Run alone it passes 17 of 17. I treated it as a likely timing flake and reran the full scoped check once. The rerun passed every step, including the rendered contrast audit and the UI smoke test. The one remaining question is whether the #0101 test flakes under load, which is a separate review-pass timing issue and not part of this task.

No human step is needed for this task. The acceptance criteria are satisfied by fixtures, and nothing here required a real device or account.

## Key learnings

Failure copy can be wrong in a way layout checks cannot see. A list that renders cleanly can still claim a state it does not know. Any `catch` that sets a list to empty should be checked for whether it turns an error into an empty history.

Fixture copy drifts from real copy. The WebKit missing-key test passed for a long time while asserting wording the server never returns. When a render test asserts a message, it should use the string the server builds, or it checks nothing about what the user sees.

The jsdom and WebKit layers answer different questions. jsdom pins the logic and the exact text, and WebKit confirms the copy fits at phone width and that the markup renders. Both were needed here.
